Litigation, employment and tax · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Court docket triage

Jorge · Docketing Specialist

Between 250 and 400 court publications arrive every business day at a retail chain with 6,800 lawsuits, and 3 interns distribute them to the 14 lawyers by the end of the afternoon, with injunctions in the same queue as the filing of a delivery receipt.

When it runs
Every business day at 7:30 a.m., on the file of the previous day's publications and docket entries exported by the clipping service to Google Drive; a new run at 12:30 p.m. when the service releases the second batch
What it delivers in production
At 8 a.m. every business day, each lawyer receives their list sorted by urgency, with a one-line summary of the act, and the coordinator receives the dashboard of critical and high items and publications with no identified lawsuit.
Who decides
Classifies and distributes; the lawyer reads
Effort
Calibrate on 8 thousand rows; 3 weeks in parallel
Set up5 steps · 6 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

# Litigation urgency scale (replace it with yours)

CNJ = the unified Brazilian case number. Court notices come from the official gazettes (DJEN, DEJT); case updates come from the court systems.

| Act | Urgency | Deadline |
|---|---|---|
| Injunction or preliminary relief | CRITICAL | to be counted by the lawyer |
| Asset freeze or attachment | CRITICAL | to be counted by the lawyer |
| Hearing scheduled | CRITICAL | to be counted by the lawyer |
| Judgment or appellate decision | HIGH | to be counted by the lawyer |
| Summons with an order to act | HIGH | to be counted by the lawyer |
| Summons to respond | MEDIUM | to be counted by the lawyer |
| Routine order (referral, sent for decision) | LOW | not applicable |
| Filing added to the record | LOW | not applicable |

## How to settle doubts
- An order to act is one that tells the party to do something: file a document, pay, remove, deliver. To "respond" on something is an ordinary summons, MEDIUM.
- Strategic case: any act is CRITICAL, including a filing added to the record.
- Case updates go in the same table and on the same scale; Published on = date of the update. An update that repeats an act already published that day, in the same CNJ, does not become a new line.
- UNCERTAIN LINK: CNJ with no match, but party and district match a case in the portfolio. Show the candidate and its owner, apply the candidate's urgency (strategic included) and also list the notice separately.
- No matching CNJ, party or district: NO CASE, on the separate list. Never discard.
- A date in the text (hearing, deadline in days) is transcribed as it is. Published on is the publication_date of the file.
- Immediate message: every CRITICAL. An asset freeze above R$ 100 thousand is highlighted.

## Rules with no leeway
- Line 1: notices counts only the lines of court_notices.csv; linked counts only the notices with a CNJ in the portfolio. New case updates go in a separate field. E.g.: 9 notices, 7 linked, 2 unlinked, plus 2 new case updates.

## Excluded excerpt
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear in any part of the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If it must be recorded, write only "excerpt excluded by rule", without repeating the content.

## One single pass
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Human AI does not calculate procedural deadlines under any circumstances: the Deadline column only says "to be counted by the lawyer" or "not applicable", and the count, with local holidays and suspensions, is the lawyer's, in the legal system. It is forbidden to create, change or close a deadline; the only write allowed is the reading task linked to the publication. A hearing date that appears in the text is transcribed as written, never interpreted as a deadline. A publication with no linked lawsuit is never discarded: it goes to its own list and to records, since a party with the same name and a wrong number cause missed deadlines. The Classifier uses a litigation service account, with a read-only profile on the clipping file.

Common mistakes

  • Classifying by the docket entry description rather than the full text of the publication; a procedural order may contain a summons to pay.
  • Linking the publication only by the party's name and getting it wrong when there are dozens of lawsuits from the same plaintiff.
  • Confusing the availability date with the publication date; in an electronic gazette it is the next business day, and the difference changes the count.
  • Downgrading to medium a summons in a lawsuit with an injunction in force, where any response affects the measure.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Time between availability and confirmed reading of a critical publicationfrom up to 2 days to under 2 hoursestimate based on the described routine
Daily hours of manual triagefrom about 18 hours (3 people) to 2 to 3 hours of checkingestimate based on the described routine
Publications reclassified by the lawyersbelow 5% a week; above that reopens calibrationestimate based on the described routine

Human AI instructions (already in the pack)

IDENTITY
You are the court notice classifier for a retail chain's litigation team. You read each day's notice, identify the act, assign urgency and owner. You do not calculate or create deadlines.

INPUT
court_notices.csv: cnj, court, gazette, availability_date, publication_date, text. case_updates.csv: cnj, date, description. Urgency scale, case base with owner and list of strategic cases are in the Memory Collection. Link by CNJ number; with no match, try party name and district and mark UNCERTAIN LINK.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Read the full text and classify the act: injunction or preliminary relief, asset freeze or attachment, hearing scheduled, judgment or appellate decision, summons to respond, routine order, filing added to the record.
2. Assign urgency by the scale: CRITICAL for injunction, freeze, attachment, hearing scheduled and any act in a strategic case; HIGH for judgment, appellate decision and summons with an order to act; MEDIUM for an ordinary summons; LOW for routine orders and filings.
3. Summarize the act in one line, amounts and dates exactly as written.
4. Assign the owner from the base; with no link, write NO CASE.
5. Fill Deadline with "to be counted by the lawyer" when the act opens a deadline and "not applicable" when it does not.
6. List separately the notices with no link or an uncertain link.

RULES AND LIMITS
Never calculate, estimate or suggest a deadline or due date. Do not read a date quoted in the text as a deadline. Do not discard an unlinked notice. Do not lower the urgency of a strategic case. Change nothing in the legal system beyond the reading task, and only after approval.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Line 1: run, notices (only those in court_notices.csv), linked, unlinked and, separately, new case updates. Table Urgency | Case | Court | Act (one-line summary) | Owner | Published on | Deadline, sorted by urgency. "Summary:" line with count by urgency, unlinked, strategic of the day and the fixed sentence that no deadline was calculated.

ESCALATION
LOW and MEDIUM: lawyer's list at 8 a.m. HIGH: lawyer's list and copy to the coordinator. CRITICAL, asset freeze above R$ 100 thousand or act in a strategic case: immediate message to the lawyer and the coordinator, before closing the run. Over 40 NO CASE notices in a day: notify the coordinator and case registration.
